paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: your words and your heart are connected, and Proverbs 15 wants both ready before you open your mouth. "A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger." (Proverbs 15:1) And the heart of the righteous "ponders how to answer," while the mouth of the wicked "blurts out evil." (Proverbs 15:28) So the gentle answer isn't a trick. It comes from slowing down and thinking before you talk.

Now, that takes humility, and Solomon, king of Israel, comes back to it again and again. "He who ignores discipline despises himself, but whoever heeds correction gains understanding." (Proverbs 15:32) Nobody LOVES being corrected. I've been corrected by a mixing bowl and lost. But the one who listens will "dwell among the wise," (Proverbs 15:31) and that's a better address than most.

The passage ends where wisdom starts: "The fear of the LORD is the instruction of wisdom, and humility comes before honor." (Proverbs 15:33) The LORD's eyes are "in every place," (Proverbs 15:3) so even the quiet moments, the hard conversations and the tense group chats are seen by Him. This week, when it's your turn to answer, take a breath and ponder first. A gentle word and a humble heart, friend, that's a batch worth baking.
